name: Light-Up Jellyfish Tank
description: Pelagia: cupped translucent jellyfish in cobalt aquarium light. Stir the water, guide a current, or tap a bell to make it pulse.

assets.credit: Original Pelagia procedural jellyfish, aquarium and light

compatibility: Canvas 2D, Path2D, Pointer Events, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, native dialog and CSS container queries. No external libraries, images, services or audio.

Mouse, touch and keyboard input. Reduced motion starts still and requires deliberate Resume. Economy reduces chain nodes, filaments, particles and canvas resolution. Hidden and offscreen canvases suspend both simulation and drawing.
Bells and filaments have bounded counts. Disposal releases arrays, listeners, observers, pointer capture, animation frames and renderer caches.
notes: Every swimmer has a short contraction and a longer recovery. Only the positive contraction derivative adds swimming thrust; bell geometry deforms from that same pulse value. Size changes the pulse period and propulsion.

Trailing tentacles and oral ribbons use independently integrated Verlet chains with fixed-distance constraints. Their delayed motion is the response of stateful linked points, not a rigid sprite or attached sine-wave texture.

Moon, lantern and ribbon forms are original artistic interpretations. The mixed population favors moon forms with cupped bells, softly scalloped skirts, short frilled arms and varied viewing angles. Resolution-independent curved membranes, translucent tissue folds and a blue-lit aquarium create depth; these are not exact biological reconstructions.

Stir the water is active by default: hover illuminates, dragging carries nearby bells and their tissue, and a tap triggers a smooth swimming contraction. Directional currents and wakes are bounded and expire after release. Light mode attracts nearby swimmers; Ambient ignores input.
Six presets, five palettes, three quality levels, a glass/open-water view, fullscreen, PNG export and Lab settings/source export are included.
reuse: JellyfishScene in model.js is DOM-free and owns pulse state, swimmer dynamics, chain constraints and local disturbances. SPECIES is a separate editable definition table.

createTankRenderer draws the scene independently; createJellyfishTank wraps it with input, responsive dimensions, lifecycle and export. Settings accept count, size range, species, palette, interaction, light and framing.
The portable source includes the full studio and a neutral embed-demo.html demonstrating an aquarium, cropped section, and hero background. Neither uses Tampa page code.
